paper.title: Retroformer: Retrospective Large Language Agents with Policy Gradient Optimization
paper.central_claim: Training a small retrospective language model with policy gradient (PPO on next-trial return change) so that its reflections, appended to a frozen actor LLM prompt, improve language agents on HotPotQA, AlfWorld and WebShop faster and further than frozen-LM self-reflection (Reflexion).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; null by design (no probing).

rationale: PPO-trained reflector credited by next-trial return; clear writer credit path, but oracle retries, single runs, one-figure untrained arm, no cost. Component_training, retained-level, scoped.

evidence.quote: learning a retrospective model, which automatically tunes the language agent prompts from environment feedback through policy gradient
evidence.support_explanation: Core operation: a trained retrospective LM rewrites actor prompt context (reflections) from environment feedback; actor stays frozen.

evidence.quote: the only learnable parameters are in the retrospective model
evidence.support_explanation: Weights updated only in the retrospective model (LoRA); the retained prompt-level artifact is the reflection text.

evidence.quote: generating useful reflective feedback from a pre-trained, frozen LLM is challenging
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: frozen-LM reflections are uninformative (credit assignment).

evidence.quote: The self-reflection responses that summarize prior failed attempts are appended to the actor prompt as the long-term memory.
evidence.support_explanation: Persistence: reflections are per-task text memory appended to the actor prompt across retries.

evidence.quote: we store the instructions and responses of the retrospective model of each trial, together with the episode returns in a local dataset, which we call replay buffer.
evidence.support_explanation: Replay buffer of (instruction, reflection, return) triples used to fine-tune the retrospective model.

evidence.quote: the difference in episode returns between two consecutive trials naturally serves as a reward signal for fine-tuning the retrospective model Mr with reinforcement learning.
evidence.support_explanation: Reward for the improver is the next-trial return change (improvement relative to previous episode).

evidence.quote: In online execution, we use best-of-n sampler, with the scores evaluated by the learned reward model
evidence.support_explanation: Inference-time compute: best-of-n with a learned reward model for the retrospective model; n not stated here.

evidence.quote: Operating under a sparse reward signal, such as binary success status (success/failure), the model detects the root cause of failure
evidence.support_explanation: The retrospective step is triggered by a success/failure signal (ground-truth correctness) at test time as in Reflexion.

evidence.quote: The agent is evaluated on 100 validation tasks from the distractor dev split of open-source HotPotQA dataset, 134 tasks in AlfWorld and 100 tasks in WebShop
to isolate the randomness of LM from the effects of reflections
evidence.support_explanation: Actor temperature 0 gives determinism, which also means no run-to-run variance is estimated.

evidence.quote: We collected 3,383 reflection samples by running the base rollout policy for 3 trials
evidence.support_explanation: Training data for HotPotQA: 3,383 reflection samples from the training set; AlfWorld 523, WebShop 267.

evidence.quote: We fine-tune the retrospective model Mr with 4-bit quantized LoRA adapters

evidence.support_explanation: An untrained (rank 0) retrospective variant appears only in the HotPotQA GPT-3 figure; no numeric table.

evidence.quote: the performance improvement by Retroformer over the frozen baselines is observed but the improvements may be limited
evidence.support_explanation: WebShop improvement is small (about 4% at four retries); authors note verbal feedback may not suit this environment.

evidence.quote: denotes the learnable parameters of each approach
evidence.support_explanation: Table reports #params, #retries and success rate for ReAct, Reflexion, SAC and Retroformer; one number per cell, no intervals.

evidence.quote: we use soft matching (e.g., f1 score) whenever possible to evaluate the alignment of the generated output with the expected answer or product as the reward function
evidence.support_explanation: Reward shaping with f1 against ground-truth answers (needs labels) for HotPotQA.

evidence.quote: This agent enhances from verbal feedback of the environment, but does not use gradient signals explicitly.
evidence.support_explanation: Reflexion baseline: uses an untrained reflector; its reflector model and sampling budget differ from Retroformer.

evidence.quote: as the Retrospective model with LONGCHAT-16 K
evidence.support_explanation: Algorithm 1 initialization line names text-davinci-003 and LongChat for the retrospective model, inconsistent with the text (LongChat only).

evidence.quote: All experiments are done in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) GKE environment with A100 40GB GPUs.
evidence.support_explanation: Compute described only as hardware type; no GPU-hours or training cost.

signatures.object: retrospective model (LongChat-7B + LoRA) that writes reflection text appended to the actor prompt
signatures.information: previous trajectory, binary/F1 episode return, persistent reflections of this task; actor weights hidden
signatures.operation: sample two reflections for a failed task, roll out the next episode with each, rate by return difference, train reward model and PPO
signatures.output: reflection text (prompt memory) and updated retrospective LoRA weights
signatures.conditions: tasks with scalar/binary return and retries; offline data from the training set
signatures.feedback: next-trial episode return minus current return
signatures.selection_rule: reward-model-scored best-of-n at inference; PPO objective with KL to reference
signatures.persistence: LoRA adapter weights (trained improver); per-task reflection memory in prompt
signatures.later_use: every retry on validation tasks reads the accumulated reflections
signatures.claimed_effect: as read from the garbled Table 2 extraction: HotPotQA 54% at 4 retries vs Reflexion 50-52%; AlfWorld 100% vs about 84-85%; WebShop +1-2 pts
signatures.failure_boundary: WebShop gains small; reflection memory is per task; uses ground-truth success signal for retries

gap.author_gap: Frozen LLM reflections are uninformative for credit assignment and language agents are not optimized with environment rewards in a gradient-compatible way.
gap.checked_gap: The fixed object is the reflector/improver (frozen or the actor itself in Reflexion); Retroformer makes it a trained small model. The weight-trained improver produces non-weight prompt edits, so the work is in scope as component_training.
gap.lineage: ReAct -> Self-Refine/Reflexion (verbal feedback, frozen reflector) -> Retroformer (RL-trained reflector); RLHF/PPO machinery from TRL.
gap.closest_adjacent: Reflexion, Self-Refine, RAP, SAC baseline; concurrent prompt-optimizer RL (not discussed).
gap.residue: Reflector quality (root-cause analysis) limits learning from failures.
gap.stakes: Figure 1 shows a looping failure produced by a frozen reflector.
gap.method_response: Learn the reflector from the return change its reflections cause.
gap.remaining_gap: Multi-environment generalization, cost, WebShop-like exploration-heavy tasks.
unresolved: no external check of more recent trained-reflector or prompt-RL papers

claims.text: Retroformer outperforms Reflexion/ReAct on HotPotQA, AlfWorld, WebShop
claims.setting: GPT-3 and GPT-4 actors, 100/134/100 validation tasks, retries up to 4
claims.selection_vs_test: reflections trained on training split; validation tasks used for reporting; retries use ground-truth success signal

claims.allowed_conclusion: Under the retry protocol, the trained reflector improves success on AlfWorld clearly and on HotPotQA modestly; WebShop gains are within noise.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Qualitative examples plus one untrained-arm curve; not a controlled credit-assignment test.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: With a ground-truth success signal for retries, a PPO-trained 7B reflector (LoRA) raises success over Reflexion with frozen reflectors on AlfWorld (100% vs 84-85%) and modestly on HotPotQA, with small WebShop effect (author-reported single runs).

retained_trace.selection: return difference ratings, reward model, PPO; best-of-n at inference
retained_trace.improver_level: partial: untrained-vs-trained reflector compared only in a HotPotQA figure

G.reason: Names a concrete residual (frozen LM reflections give poor credit assignment, Fig 1 example) against Reflexion/Self-Refine/RAP with a feature table; additional trained-reflector or prompt-RL neighbors are not covered, and gradient-compatibility is partly motivation.

M.reason: Using the next-trial return change of paired reflection rollouts as reward for a reward model/PPO is a coherent mechanism with a clear credit path; weak spots are the low-signal ratings when returns stay at 0 and the formulation/Algorithm inconsistency.

X.reason: Data collection counts, LoRA ranks, SFT+reward-model+PPO pipeline and prompts are described, with the writer-reader interface clear; inference best-of-n size, memory length handling and consistency of the algorithm listing are unclear, and no retention gate/versioning exists.

E.measurement.reason: Standard task success rates on three public environments, with rewards computed from ground truth; test-time retry uses the success signal, and metric definition for HotPotQA success is not spelled out.

E.causality.reason: ReAct/Reflexion/SAC baselines and an untrained r=0 arm only in one HotPotQA figure; no ablation of the reward model, SFT, reward shaping or best-of-n, no budget-matched Reflexion, and Reflexion uses a different reflector model.

E.holdout.reason: Training tasks are separate from validation tasks, but retries on validation tasks use the ground-truth success signal (A2: oracle retry), reflector selection details are not given and the only transferred asset is a reflector trained on the same three environments.

E.statistics.reason: Task counts are stated and WebShop limitation is acknowledged, but each cell is one deterministic run (temperature 0) with no intervals or seeds; HotPotQA/WebShop margins are 1-4 points on 100 tasks.

E.cost.reason: Parameter counts and sample counts are given but no training compute, rollout cost or inference best-of-n cost; baselines are not cost-matched.
